items.t: "Chilliwack Proper East" is a board (CADREB) sub-area name for the eastern part of Chilliwack Proper in the City of Chilliwack. Municipally, the same ground sits inside the OCP's Schedule B2 "Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan" area; the City does not use "Chilliwack Proper East" as a planning name in the sources opened. Street-level board boundary: Not verified — CADREB publishes no street-level boundary for the sub-area in the public sources used.

Rebuild note carried from the audit record: the Oct 21, 2026 thin-content audit records the Proper East page as mostly duplicate of chilliwack-proper-south.html (64.0%) — a flag about the pages' copy, not a fact about the neighbourhood.

Where the condo stock concentrates: the Yale Road corridor east of downtown. All four verified apartment-condo buildings in stand on Yale Road (46289, 46693, 46777 and 46966 Yale Road). The rest of the live feed is detached houses (ranchers and older houses on full-size lots, including on McNaught Road, First Avenue and Second Avenue), one multi-level townhouse unit on Hazel Street, a half-duplex with a basement suite on James Street, a bungalow on Cleveland Avenue, and land listings — houses, strata units and vacant lots in one feed.
Schools: Chilliwack is SD33.

Agriculture at the eastern edge: the City states agriculture accounts for 67% of the City's total land base and 29% of economic activity; ALR status for any specific parcel is a parcel-by-parcel check.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Chilliwack Proper East

items.t: OCP: Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500 — current: The City's city-wide plan, including protection of the Agricultural Land Reserve; this ground sits in its Schedule B2 "Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan," with the Schedule D development permit areas (D-1 Drinking Water Supply, D-2 Hillside Environment, D-3 Riparian Area, D-4 Farm Home Plate, D-5 Hillside Development, D-6 Downtown, D-7 Mixed-Use Areas, D-8 Residential, D-9 Commercial, D-10 Industrial) applying per parcel — which areas apply to a given parcel is a per-parcel check, not verified for any specific lot here.
Zoning: Chilliwack Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000: — the parcel's actual zone is confirmed with the City per parcel.

SSMUH (Bylaw 5395, adopted Jun 18, 2024): Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 2024, No. 5395, amending Bylaw 5000, allows 3 to 4 dwelling units on parcels within the urban growth boundary zoned for single-detached and duplex housing. Added-unit permission is NOT permission to subdivide and does not create new lots.

Secondary suites and accessory units (Bylaw 5000): a secondary suite is an accessory dwelling unit of not more than 90 m² and less than 40% of the habitable floor space of the building — the lesser of 90 m² and 40% (s.2); only 1 accessory dwelling unit may be located on a lot, and the permitted ADU types include secondary suite, coach house and garden suite (s.4.06(1)); garden suites are capped at a maximum gross floor area of 100 m² (s.4.06(1)(g)); ADU parking is 1 space for a 1-bedroom ADU or any secondary suite and 2 spaces for a 2-or-more-bedroom coach or garden suite (s.5.04). No secondary suite is legal unless built with a building permit meeting the BC Building and Fire Code and current flood protection requirements, and new suites are not permitted below the flood construction level.

ALR block (provincial frame, for any ALR parcel at the sub-area's edge): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tier — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by Oct 31 — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR, and no farm-class claim is asserted for any parcel here.

Chilliwack property taxes (2026): notices mailed at the end of May, due the first working day after July 1; a 5% penalty applies to taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026, and an additional 5% to taxes outstanding after August 4, 2026.

Foreclosure / court-sale note: Where a court sale is met, the settled process is the BC Supreme Court process (Rules 21-7/13-5, PD-66, Form 60), with Form B availability and the PTT/GST treatment of court sales not confirmed and kept distinct from the GI-003 frame above.

blocks.text: Good to know about Chilliwack Proper East

items.t: The page contradicts itself on zoning — in its own feed. The editorial copy describes lots of 6,000 to 8,000 sq ft with "R1-A duplex or R1-B small-lot subdivision potential," while one of its own feed cards describes a Lewis Avenue lot "rezoned from R 1-A to R 1-C" for a two-lot subdivision — listing text and editorial text pointing at different zone labels for the same ground.
Two Quarry Road names in Proper East searches are not Proper East land.

A bus route moved one block — and it matters for two feed streets. Effective January 4, 2026, Route 57 Broadway's Carleton Street service shifted one block east to McNaught Road, with new stops on McNaught and Acorn — the same McNaught Road that carries this sub-area's detached and land listings.

The suite cap is a "lesser of," not a choice. Chilliwack's suite ceiling is the lesser of 90 m² and 40% of the building's habitable floor space, only one ADU is permitted per lot in total, and garden suites cap separately at 100 m² — a lot marketed with both a suite and a coach house in mind is priced on a permission Bylaw 5000 does not give.

Agriculture is the city's land base, even on its urban east side. The City states agriculture accounts for 67% of Chilliwack's total land base and 29% of its economic activity — the reason ALR status is a per-parcel check even for ground that reads as city lots, and why the OCP's D-4 Farm Home Plate permit area exists in the Schedule D list.

Page-defect check: the defects documented in this area's own research are (1) the 64.0% duplication of chilliwack-proper-south.html (Oct 21, 2026 audit) and (2) the editorial/feed zone-label conflict carried above.

faq.a: Yes — four verified apartment-condo buildings, all on Yale Road: Newmark (46289 Yale Road, 228 units, 2008), Mountain View Estates (46966 Yale Road, 55+ in listings), Evergreen Estates (46777 Yale Road, 22 units, 1993) and an unnamed 55+-described building at 46693 Yale Road (built 1996 in its listing).
faq.q: Are there any condos in Chilliwack Proper East?

faq.a: The Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 5500 — specifically Schedule B2, the Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan, with Schedule D development permit areas applying per parcel.
faq.q: Which plan governs Chilliwack Proper East?

faq.a: The building is presented as a 55+ community. A 55+ bylaw is the one age bylaw BC law still allows (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2), with exemptions for legacy residents, live-in caregivers and (since May 1, 2023) younger spouses/partners and defined children — whether you can occupy, or only own and rent, depends on the registered bylaw on the Form B.
faq.q: Can I buy in Mountain View Estates if I am under 55?

faq.a: No. Mountain View Estates and Evergreen Estates both carry "rentals not allowed" directory lines, and long-term rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC. Their pet lines (pets not allowed in both directories) are a different matter — pet bylaws remain enforceable and are confirmed on the Form B.
faq.q: The directories say two buildings here ban rentals — is that current?

faq.a: Yes. The five-year depreciation-report duty since July 1, 2024 applies to stratas with five or more lots; at 8 units Thornberry Lane is over the threshold, and it cannot defer by vote.
faq.q: Thornberry Lane has only 8 units — does the depreciation-report rule still apply?

faq.a: The Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 5500 — specifically Schedule B2, the Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan.
faq.q: Which plan governs Proper East, and which schedule is it?

faq.a: No — only 1 accessory dwelling unit per lot where the zone permits: a secondary suite (capped at the lesser of 90 m² and 40% of habitable floor space), a coach house, or a garden suite (capped at 100 m²), under Bylaw 5000. Separately, SSMUH (Bylaw 5395, adopted June 18, 2024) allows 3–4 units on eligible urban-growth-boundary parcels zoned single-detached/duplex.
faq.q: Can a Proper East house add a suite and a coach house?
Is there an official median price for Chilliwack Proper East?
faq.a: No figure is stated in this file: Chilliwack is a CADREB market that the SnapStats extraction used by this program does not cover, and CADREB publishes no area statistics in the sources used, so no median, sales ratio or inventory figure for this sub-area exists in these sources (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report, coverage limit).

faq.q: Which plan covers Chilliwack Proper East?
faq.a: The Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan, which guides residential infill development and is now Schedule B2 of Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500; it was first added to the 2040 OCP as Schedule D through Bylaw 2018, No. 4533.

faq.q: Which schools are near Chilliwack Proper East?
faq.a: Bernard Elementary (45465 Bernard Ave), Robertson Elementary (46106 Southlands Cres) and Strathcona Elementary (46375 Strathcona Rd), all Kindergarten to Grade 5, plus Chilliwack Middle School (46354 Yale Rd, Grades 6 to 8) and Chilliwack Secondary (46363 Yale Rd, Grades 9 to 12) — names and addresses confirmed against the BC Ministry K-12 file; catchments are set by address, so confirm a specific address with the SD33 School Locator (~/workspace/area-research-2026-11/education/work/bc_k12_schools.csv, read 2026-11-01).
